text:
alice: Customer ACME reports regressions after tonight's rollout — a bunch of function/tool calls are either missing or have scrambled args. They sent examples where charge_card got amount and currency swapped and some requests returned free text instead of a tool call. Can someone take?

ben: @carla can you take a look? sounds like a post-process/parsing issue rather than model hallucination. :eyes:

carla: looking. any sample payloads or logs?

alice: pasted their minimal repro (redacted IDs):
```
POST /v1/chat
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-v2",
  "input": "Charge user for order 123",
  "tools": [{"name":"charge_card","schema":{"amount":"float","currency":"str","card_id":"str"}}]
}
```
And the runtime extracted this toolcall from the assistant channel:
```
{"tool":"charge_card","args":{"currency":100.0,"amount":"USD","card_id":"card_abc"}}
```
So the numeric amount ended up in the currency field and vice-versa.

dave: ACME also reported intermittent missing calls — sometimes the assistant returns: "Payment processed" free text and no toolcall event. They first noticed right after the rollout at ~23:00 UTC.

deploy-bot: deploy notification: "deploy/redwood-chat-v2 rollout started 1950012200 -> completed 1950012300; variant-swap at 1950012245; canary 10% -> ramped"

carla: thanks. initial hypothesis: a serialization/deserialization path changed in the new runtime that maps positional outputs into args incorrectly when the model emits arrays instead of objects. Also fallback parser may be stricter and dropping toolcalls when parsing fails.

ben: can you reproduce locally? if it's the parser, quick patch might be possible.

carla: repro steps I ran: used the exact ACME prompt + model snapshot + new runtime flag "--strict-tool-json" and I see both behaviors: (1) model sometimes emits: `["charge_card", 100.0, "USD", "card_abc"]` vs the expected object; (2) our mapper assumed object ordering and assigned keys by index, leading to amount<->currency swap. Also on parse errors we fall back to assistant_text instead of emitting an error event.

carla: minimal repro command: `python tools/repro_toolcall.py --model redwood-chat-v2 --prompt "Charge user" --seed 42 --runtime v2`. Output logged as above.

ben: ok actionable list?

alice: customer is asking for rollback or ETA. They're escalated with account team.

carla: proposed immediate actions: 1) roll customer traffic back to redwood-chat-v1 or pin to previous runtime variant for that org (quick). 2) patch mapper to accept both object and array forms and map using schema names when available (hotfix). 3) make parser emit a visible error event and avoid silent fallback so we can surface to telemetry. 4) add unit/e2e tests with ACME prompt set and run canary.

ben: agree. who owns rollback and telemetry? @deploy-bot can assist with per-org pinning but need SRE/ops to apply.

deploy-bot: ops runbook: call `ops pin-variant --org acme --model redwood-chat-v1 --until 2025-10-12T06:00Z` to pin. Manual approval required for org-level pin.

carla: ETA: hotfix + unit tests ~3 hours, canary + validation ~1 hour. I can push patch to a hotfix branch now.

alice: I'll tell ACME we can pin them immediately and that eng is working on a fix with an ETA. Offering credits.

dave: please add a quick eval job that checks both object and list emissions against the tool schema across the v2 snapshot. We should catch this on future rollouts.

carla: will add tests and a guard in the rollout pipeline to run that eval before variant-swap.

alice: thanks team. I'll update the ticket and coordinate the rollback for ACME now.

ben: follow-ups: postmortem + checklist item for toolcall-serialization testing. assigning to eng-runtime to own.

carla: starting patch now, will post PR link in this thread when ready.

alice: thx — keep me posted.
